title: The Water in This Cloud Weighs 500 Tonnes
pause_note: Short format v3: 20-30 s, claim first, loop ending

beats: The water in this cloud weighs five hundred tonnes.
A puffy cloud a kilometre across holds about half a gram of water in each cubic metre.
Over a billion cubic metres, that adds up to five hundred tonnes.
It floats because the droplets are tiny, so they fall very slowly, and rising air holds them up.
